The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(2)$ where $h(x)=f(x)-g(x).$
worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)-{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(2)={f}^{′}(2)-{g}^{′}(2).
$$

Also, notice that $x=2$ corresponds to 

- the interval $x\in (-2,3)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (-2,3)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039683/assets/299b996bf08e4b4e8560d013829ddd1f42751767cd3f00dcd04c23c95f2c62b4.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{1-1}{3-(-2)}=0.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(2)=0.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (-2,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{3-(-2)}{3-(-2)}=1.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(2)=1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & ={f}^{′}(2)-{g}^{′}(2) \\  & =0-1 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
